text:
Tomas Hertl plays his 900th NHL game tonight in San Jose, the building where most of them happened. The Sharks drafted him 17th overall in 2012 and traded him to Vegas in March 2024. He has nine points in four games against them since, and his chances lately have been as dangerous as any depth forward's: 4.7 expected goals (the quality of the shots he's getting) in his last 10 games, from third-line minutes. He's one of our Sleepers tonight, at 29% to score.

The Sharks come home from a 7-0 loss in Anaheim, where Laurent Brossoit stopped all 23 shots. They've been outscored 22-12 over their last five, and Thanksgiving brought changes: Cam Lund and Luca Cagnoni recalled, Brett Leason and Libor Hajek sent down. Ryan Warsofsky didn't commit to either recall playing, but told reporters, per Sharks Hockey Digest's Max Miller, "when you're not playing well, there's going to be decisions that we'll have to make to improve our team." Jacob Trouba, Kiefer Sherwood and Igor Chernyshov are out, and Ivar Stenberg has taken Chernyshov's spot beside Macklin Celebrini and Will Smith.

Vegas is 2-1-2 in its last five, but it won the chance battle in all five, and the 5-3 win in Edmonton came with a three-point night from rookie Trevor Connelly, who leads all rookies in points, as The Athletic's Jesse Granger noted. Mark Stone has passed into first on the franchise's career points list this month, and Jack Eichel carries a five-game point streak. Noah Hanifin is off ESPN's injury report and could return.

Our numbers have Vegas at 3.83 expected goals and San Jose at 2.78. The special-teams gap is the one to watch: the Sharks take 4.4 penalties a game, and their penalty kill allows 0.95 expected goals a game against a Vegas power play that makes 0.78. Yaroslav Askarov is 2.9 goals better than expected this season after a rough last year; Carter Hart is just under even. In the Pacific, Vegas is 11 points clear of San Jose.
headline: Tomas Hertl brings 900 games back to San Jose
